evals.prompt: Design the Markdown content model from docs/product/specs/markdown-content-model.md. The codebase map is in docs/engineering/architecture.md.
evals.expected_output: A design at docs/engineering/designs/markdown-content-model.md with components mapped to REQs, the content schema in the framework's own form citing its documentation and version, routes and generated artifacts as contracts, build and render flows with a failure path per EDGE, ADRs for decisions with viable alternatives, a verification plan with one row per AC, and check_design.py reporting ok, its first and final run quoted whole in the reply (or one quote when the first run was already ok) and the final one recorded in docs/engineering/designs/markdown-content-model.check.json; user-owned decisions asked, not assumed. This case uses the live web: a failing run is read with the network of that day in mind.
assertions: Every REQ, NFR, EDGE and AC id from the specification appears in the design; docs/engineering/designs/markdown-content-model.check.json records "ok": true for this specification and this design; and the reply quotes the check_design.py command and the whole JSON line of a run reporting "ok": true (when the first run was already ok and nothing changed after it, that one quote counts as the final run)

Every framework API named in the design either cites a documentation URL with the version read, or a file in the codebase, or is listed under 'Assumptions to verify before implementation' with how to verify it
Each ADR has at least two options with consequences and names the requirement ids it serves
The verification plan has one concrete check per acceptance criterion
No decision classified as the user's is made silently; such decisions appear as questions with a recommendation

evals.prompt: Design the search architecture. The spec is in docs/product/specs/search.md but it still has an open question about the provider.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the spec, finds the OPEN that blocks the provider component, and stops with at most three questions with recommended answers instead of designing around a guessed provider; nothing is written to docs/engineering/designs/.

assertions.text: No design file is written while the blocking OPEN is unresolved

assertions: The user is asked at most three questions, each with a recommended answer

The reply names OPEN-1 of the specification as what blocks the design, and the question about the provider recommends the specification's own answer: an index generated at build time and searched in the browser

evals.prompt: Run the traceability check on the design docs/engineering/designs/expense-export.md against its specification, docs/product/specs/expense-export.md, and fix what it flags.
evals.expected_output: The first run of check_design.py, quoted in the reply, reports REQ-2 and AC-2 missing from the design, AC-2 without a verification row, and ADR 0001 with a single option. The fixes add a component for REQ-2 (the rows of the file: columns, two decimals, sorted by date) and a verification row for AC-2 with its input and expected output. REQ-3 and the ADR's own Context say the CSV format is fixed by the requirement and no alternative was considered, so the ADR is not a decision: docs/engineering/adr/0001-export-file-format.md is removed (git status --short in the reply shows it deleted), the design no longer cites ADR-0001 and its Decisions row gives the format as decided by REQ-3; no second option is invented. The final run, quoted in the reply and recorded in docs/engineering/designs/expense-export.check.json, reports ok: true.
assertions: The reply quotes the check's first run (its JSON output or its findings as printed), made before any fix: REQ-2 and AC-2 missing from the design, AC-2 without a verification row, and the ADR with only one option

The component added for REQ-2 states the row contract of the specification (the columns date, payee, category and amount, amounts with two decimals, rows sorted by date, oldest first), and the verification row added for AC-2 names a concrete check with an input and the expected output, not `manual`

The single-option ADR is removed, not completed with an invented second option: the final run's JSON line in the reply lists no ADR (`"adrs": []`), or docs/engineering/designs/expense-export.check.json counts no ADR (`"adrs": 0`), or the reply's `git status --short` shows docs/engineering/adr/0001-export-file-format.md as deleted; the design no longer cites ADR-0001; and the design states the CSV format as decided by REQ-3
The reply quotes the check's final run (its command and its JSON output) reporting "ok": true, and docs/engineering/designs/expense-export.check.json records "ok": true

evals.prompt: We're offline today, so no docs sites: design the Markdown content model from docs/product/specs/markdown-content-model.md with what's in the repo. The codebase map is in docs/engineering/architecture.md.
evals.expected_output: Without web access the design takes the framework's version from package.json (Astro, at the version written there) and cites no documentation URL; every framework API it names (the content collection definition, its loader, the schema helper, the functions that list entries and build static paths) is listed under 'Assumptions to verify before implementation' with how to verify it; the report says the web was not available and that versions come from package.json; check_design.py still runs, and its record says ok.
assertions: The design names the Astro version exactly as package.json gives it, and says that the version comes from package.json
Neither the design nor the reply cites a documentation URL for a framework or library API
Every framework API the design names is listed under 'Assumptions to verify before implementation', each with how to verify it
docs/engineering/designs/markdown-content-model.check.json is among the files the run produced, its `ok` is true, and the reply quotes the JSON line of that run
